boundaries_touched.review: opencode (FORNX-161) is the third provider integration and a genuinely distinct shape: an in-process JS/TS plugin (@opencode-ai/plugin) opencode's own runtime invokes synchronously, spawning a long-lived companion binary (fornax-hook-opencode) fed one NDJSON line per hook over stdin, rather than an external hook-script process (Claude Code) or a rollout-file tail (Codex). Reviewed OpenCodeAdapter::translate/probe (crates/fornax-adapter-opencode/src/lib.rs): RuntimeCapabilities values are always a fixed declaration returned by probe(), never derived from the native payload, so a payload cannot claim a capability the adapter doesn't implement; a missing/unknown hook shape returns Unrecognized/Ignored rather than panicking; CollectionMethod/provenance strings are hardcoded per sensor at construction time, never interpolated from untrusted payload content in their trust-relevant part. No new Cargo dependency (all workspace-pinned) and no new npm dependency (plugin/fornax-capture.js uses only the node:child_process builtin, no package.json). One High finding surfaced while reviewing this boundary is recorded under evidence_provenance below (its root cause, a provider-controlled session_id, is introduced here but its impact is on the daemon's capability cache, not payload parsing itself).

boundaries_touched.review: SEC-v0.0.3-0002 (High, fixed in PR TBD): fornax-daemon's in-memory state.caps cache (crates/fornax-daemon/src/main.rs handle_message) was a single HashMap<session_id, RuntimeCapabilities> slot with no provider check, but session_id is provider-controlled data (an adapter reads it straight off its native payload, e.g. opencode's /input/sessionID). A same-session Capabilities announcement from a different provider than the one already cached silently overwrote it in-memory -- the exact slot the Claim handler reads to gate every verifier -- a real cross-provider capability downgrade that could suppress verification and hide evidence, matching FORNX-244's 'capability spoofing/downgrade' focus item verbatim. The persisted store was never affected: Store::upsert_capabilities is correctly scoped to (session_id, provider) (crates/fornax-store/src/lib.rs), one row per announcing provider. Fixed by refusing to overwrite an already-cached session's in-memory capability snapshot from a different provider than the one already cached, logging a warning instead.
boundaries_touched.adversarial_coverage: crates/fornax-daemon/src/main.rs::tests::cross_provider_capabilities_announcement_does_not_clobber_cached_session -- proven non-vacuous by reverting the provider-match guard (recreating the pre-fix unconditional cache.insert(sid, caps)) and confirming the test fails with the ClaudeCode session's FinalResponse capability downgraded to Unavailable by the spoofed OpenCode announcement, then restoring the fix and confirming the test passes

boundaries_touched.review: First real content in this previously-placeholder boundary. plugin/fornax-capture.js is a real @opencode-ai/plugin Plugin that opencode's own runtime loads in-process -- the inverse trust direction from Claude Code/Codex, which never load Fornax code into their own process. Reviewed the plugin end to end: it is transport-only (JSON-encodes each hook's input/output verbatim to fornax-hook-opencode's stdin), never eval/requires/executes anything derived from a hook payload, and never rewrites tool args despite opencode's API allowing it. fornax-hook-opencode is resolved by bare name off PATH and spawned once at plugin init inside opencode's own process -- same trust class as the pre-existing informational adapter_provider_input finding (no privilege boundary crossed, runs as the invoking user). FORNX-161's two disclosed failure modes were verified fixed in the reviewed code, not merely claimed: (1) an unhandled 'error' event on the spawned ChildProcess was a fatal, uncaught exception in the parent process (opencode itself, since the plugin runs in-process) when fornax-hook-opencode isn't on PATH -- child.on('error', ...) and child.stdin.on('error', ...) listeners now swallow it (plugin/fornax-capture.js lines 31-39); (2) dispose() now awaits child.stdin.end()'s callback, bounded by a 200ms timeout so a dead/hung child can never delay opencode's own shutdown, closing the race that could previously drop the last queued event on fast shutdown (lines 56-70). No Jira Bug is needed for either -- both are already fixed, with the fix present in the exact code reviewed for this candidate.
boundaries_touched.adversarial_coverage: crates/fornax-adapter-opencode/tests/live_transport.rs drives the real plugin/fornax-capture.js file (loaded and invoked exactly as opencode's runtime would) through a real fornax-hook-opencode process and a real fornax-daemon over a live Unix domain socket -- this is the automated regression for the FORNX-291 transport leg; the error-listener and dispose-flush fixes themselves are point fixes confirmed present by direct code review (plugin/fornax-capture.js lines 31-39, 56-70) rather than a dedicated crash-reproduction test, since reproducing a fatal uncaught-exception-in-the-host-process scenario safely in CI is not practical -- recorded here as a real, disclosed limitation, not rounded up to a full non-vacuity proof
